## Three Surprising Facts About the Roman Empire

1. **The Roman Empire lasted far longer than most people think.** The Western Roman Empire fell in 476 AD, but the Eastern Roman Empire (the Byzantine Empire) continued for nearly another **thousand years**, finally falling in 1453 AD — the same year as the invention of the Gutenberg printing press.

2. **Romans used urine as mouthwash and a laundry detergent.** The ammonia in aged urine made it effective for whitening teeth and cleaning clothes. It was so commercially valuable that Emperor Vespasian actually imposed a **tax on urine collection**, giving rise to the Latin saying *"Pecunia non olet"* ("Money doesn't stink").

3. **September through December are named for the wrong months.** The original Roman calendar had only **10 months**, so September (from *septem*, 7), October (*octo*, 8), November (*novem*, 9), and December (*decem*, 10) were accurately named. When January and February were added, the names were never updated — leaving us with a permanent numerical mismatch we still use today.
